record.paper_title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems
record.original_question: In heterogeneous computing applications that are decomposed into tasks and subtasks, what methods can support the feedback communications required among subtasks?

evidence.quote: It is also assumed that some tasks may be further decomposed into two or more communicating subtasks. The subtasks have data dependencies among them, but are able to be assigned to different machines for execution.
Methods for allowing feedback communications among subtasks tasks are necessary.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a heterogeneous computing environment consisting of a set of machines $M = \{m_1, \ldots, m_k\}$ with differing architectures, capabilities, and interconnection networks. An application is modeled as a directed graph $G = (T, E)$ whose nodes are tasks; each task $t \in T$ may itself be decomposed into a set of communicating subtasks $S_t = \{s_{t,1}, \ldots, s_{t,n_t}\}$ with data dependencies among them, and individual subtasks may be assigned to different machines in $M$ for execution. In contrast to purely feed-forward (one-way) data dependencies, allow bidirectional dependencies in which the output of a subtask $s_{t,j}$ may need to be returned as input to a previously executed (or concurrently executing) subtask $s_{t,i}$, possibly on a different machine, during the course of task execution.

Develop and characterize methods (including programming-model abstractions, scheduling/assignment policies, runtime communication mechanisms, and synchronization protocols) that support such feedback communications among subtasks of a decomposed application in a heterogeneous computing system. Specifically: (i) define a formal model of subtask feedback communication that extends standard task-graph models to allow cyclic data dependencies; (ii) design mapping and scheduling algorithms for such models that account for inter-machine communication latencies and heterogeneous compute costs; and (iii) determine conditions under which feedback-aware mappings can be produced efficiently and analyze their performance relative to feedback-oblivious mappings.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad open research direction concerning runtime and scheduling support for feedback (cyclic) dependencies among subtasks in heterogeneous computing. While many partial techniques exist (DAG schedulers such as HEFT, dataflow runtimes like StarPU, Legion, and Charm++ that support iterative/feedback patterns), no single accepted solution to the general formulation is documented. Available evidence is inconclusive about a definitive resolution.
